newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas seen driven higher again by cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas seen driven higher again by cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open higher Wednesday, propped up again by firmer cash and a strong demand in the Southwest, market sources said.

May over-the-counter trade crept up to about $2.19-2.20 by 0935 EDT after beginning at $2.15-2.19. The contract, set to expire Thursday, settled at $2.114 per million British thermal units on Tuesday.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked about 10 cents higher in the low-$2.20s.
In ACCESS, May last traded 5.1 cents higher at $2.165.
Technical traders said next resistance was at $2.21 after May climbed past $2.16 in ACCESS. May support was seen at $2.09, and then at $2.035, $1.925 and $1.88.
Taking a look ahead, resistance in June was pegged at the $2.21-2.23 gap from mid-January, while support was seen at $2.085 and then along the short-term up trendline at $1.98.

In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly at $2.04-2.09. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted in the mid-$2.30s.
Early estimates for today's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from a draw of 32 bcf to a build of 30 bcf, versus a gain last year of 27 bcf.
